r0010: The European Court of Human Rights (Third Section), sitting as a Chamber composed of:
r0011:
Mr	G. Ress, President,
	Mr	L. Caflisch,
	Mr	P. Kūris,
	Mr	R. Türmen,
	Mr	J. Hedigan,
	Mrs	H.S. Greve,
	Mr	K. Traja, judges,
and Mr V. Berger, Section Registrar,
r0012: Having deliberated in private on 2 October 2003,
r0013: Delivers the following judgment, which was adopted on that date:
r0015: 1.  The case originated in an application (no. 53431/99) against the Republic of Turkey lodged with the Court under Article 34 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (“the Convention”) by a Turkish national, Binali Gençel (“the applicant”), on 17 September 1999.
r0016: 2.  The applicant was represented by Ms Z.S. Özdoğan, a lawyer practising in Izmir. The Turkish Government (“the Government”) did not designate an Agent for the purposes of the proceedings before the Court.
r0017: 3.  On 7 November 2000 the Court (First Section) decided to communicate the application to the Government.
r0018: 4.  By a letter of 18 November 2002, the Court informed the parties that, in accordance with Article 29 §§ 1 and 3 of the Convention, it would rule on both the admissibility and the merits of the application.
